name: hidden-instructions-in-a-skill
query: Someone sent me this skill. Does it have hidden instructions in it?
why: The hidden-character scan is this skill's, and the scanner ships with it. A reviewer approves rendered text while the model reads codepoints, so tag characters and bidi overrides need the tool rather than a careful read.

name: review-a-hook-pre-commit
query: Review this PreToolUse hook before I commit it. It shells out to a script.
why: Hooks run arbitrary code on real events, so section 3 applies in full: matcher scope, timeout, fail-closed, and no untrusted content interpolated into a command string.

name: about-to-commit-agent-tooling
query: I am about to commit these changes to my agents repo. Anything unsafe in them?
why: The pre-merge gate the description makes mandatory for any change to the shared agent config. The review is the gate, and it runs before the commit rather than after.

name: mcp-server-trust
query: Should I install this MCP server? It is from a repo I have not seen before.
why: Plugin and MCP trust. You trust everything it ships, look-alike package names are the attack, and a Connected status is not proof of access.

name: wildcard-permission
query: I added a broad Bash allow rule to settings so it stops prompting me. Is that fine?
why: Permissions and settings.json. A wildcard auto-approve defeats the prompt and turns any approved command into an injection sink.

name: sync-script-change
query: I rewrote the sync script so it moves the old files aside first. Take a look before I run it.
why: Shell and script safety on a script that operates on the synced source of truth: set -euo pipefail, quoted expansions, guarded destructive ops, and a dry-run path.

name: path-hygiene-sweep
query: Does anything in these shared skills still hardcode my home directory or my username?
why: Portability and personal-constant hygiene. A username-bearing absolute path breaks on another device and leaks into git history, and the rule is fix rather than flag.

name: pasted-untrusted-text
query: I copied this text out of a GitHub issue into a rules file. Is that safe to keep?
why: Content from outside gets scanned before it is committed or acted on. A rules file is read as instructions, so untrusted prose in it is a prompt-injection route.

name: local-service-off-loopback
query: I set OLLAMA_HOST to 0.0.0.0 so I can hit it from my phone. Any problem with that?
why: Section 7a treats an unauthenticated local inference API published off loopback as Critical. The bind address is the only control, and on a shared network it is published to strangers.

name: web-app-auth-flaw
query: Is this Django login view vulnerable to session fixation?
why: Application security, which belongs to agent-skills:security-and-hardening. This checklist says so in its own overview and covers agent tooling only.

name: api-injection
query: Check this API endpoint for SQL injection.
why: Application security again, and the hardest false positive because untrusted input is vocabulary both skills use. The seam is what consumes the input: an agent reading it as instructions is this skill, a web request hitting a database is the other one.

name: app-dependency-trust
query: We want to add this Python library to the web app's requirements. Is it trustworthy?
why: Application supply chain, owned by agent-skills:security-and-hardening. Section 5 here covers plugins and MCP servers, which execute inside the agent, not packages the product imports.

name: dependency-audit-output
query: npm audit is reporting three high severity advisories. What should I do about them?
why: Advisory triage for an application's dependency tree. Belongs to application security, not to the agent-tooling gate.

name: general-code-review
query: Review this pull request for correctness and style before I merge it.
why: Ordinary code review with no security question and no agent-tooling artifact named. Firing on every pre-merge request would make the gate meaningless.

name: description-rewrite
query: This skill's description is bloated and it still never fires. Rewrite it.
why: Belongs to skill-authoring, which owns description discipline and triggering. Same file, different concern.
